textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternative. 1. What is the primary source of energy for all living organisms in an ecosystem? a. Temperature b. Pressure c. Sunlight d. Rainfall 2. What is the role of decomposers in ecosystems? a. They convert inorganic compounds into organic matter. b. They obtain energy from sunlight. c. They convert dead and decaying matter into simple inorganic compounds. d. They produce food though photosynthesis. 3. Which of the following is an example of mutualism? a. Tiger and deer b. Mosquito and human c. Rhizobium bacteria and leguminous plant d. Frog and insect 4. What is the term for the linear arrangement of trophic levels in an ecosystem where energy flows? a. Energy web b. Food web c. Trophic hierarchy d. Food chain 5. What is nudation in the process of succession? a. The migration of seeds to a bare area b. The establishment of a species in a bare area. c. The modification of environment by living organisms. d. The formation of a bare area by natural or human causes. 6. What is the first biological community that develops in a bare are called? a. Climax community b. Intermediate community c. Pioneer community d. Stable community 7. Which of the following best defines nitrogen fixation? a. The conversion of atmospheric oxygen into nitrogeneous compounds b. The conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically acceptable forms. c. The conversion of soil nitrogen into atmospheric nitrogen. d. The conversion of nitrogen compounds into atmospheric gases. 8. What is the role of nitrifying bacteria in the nitrogen cycle? a. They convert atmospheric nitrogen into usable forms. b. They convert ammonia ammonia into nitrites and nitrates. c. They convert intrites and nitrates into atmospherc nitrogen. d. They convert organic nitrogen into ammonia.

B. Answer the following questions: 1. Who coined the ‘ecology’? Define the term. 2. Explain the importance of sunlight in an ecosystem. 3. How does temperature affect plant and animal life in an ecosystem? 4. What role does rainfall play in determining vegetation types in an ecosystem? 5. Define positive interaction. Differentiate between mutualism and protocooperation. 6. Explain the concept of predation and provide an example. 7. How do intraspecific interactions differ from interspecific interaction? 8. What are the structural components of a pond ecosystem, and how do they contribute to its functioning? 9. What is succession? Describe the types and process of succession. 10. What is biogeochemical cycle? Describe nitrogen cycle in detail. ***** Biology, Grade 11 | 204
